metadata.title: The Butcher's Debt
metadata.description: You wake on the concrete floor of a walk-in freezer, breath crystallizing in front of you. Beyond the heavy steel door, a butcher whistles while he works. Sal Morano thinks you saw something you shouldn't have — and in this part of Chicago, witnesses don't make it to morning. Find a way out before you become tomorrow's special.
metadata.author: ai-generated

setting.ambient_text: The freezer hums. Your breath hangs in the air like ghosts. Through the insulated walls, you hear whistling — something cheerful, obscene against the cold. A cleaver hits a cutting board. Again. Again.

items.name: Meat Hook
items.description: A heavy steel hook, sharp at the tip. Used for hanging carcasses.

then.text: Solid steel, maybe eight inches. The curve is sharp enough to gouge. The base has a flat end — could pry things.
Heavy. Cold. You grip it like a weapon. The curved end could hook onto things or pry them apart.

items.name: Bloodstained Apron
items.description: Sal's work apron. The stains tell stories.

then.text: White cotton, brown with old blood. A pocket on the front. Something stiff inside it.
You fish in the pocket. A crumpled receipt — Moretti's Hardware, dated last Tuesday. Someone bought 200 lbs of quickite. The four-digit order number is circled: 1-9-5-3.
Nothing else in the pockets. Just the stink of old blood.
A filthy work apron. You already found the receipt in its pocket.

items.name: Hardware Receipt
items.description: A receipt from Moretti's Hardware. Order #1953.

then.text: Moretti's Hardware & Supply. 200 lbs quickite (calcium oxide powder). Order #1953. Paid cash. A handwritten note in the margin: 'Back office — Tony says use the order number.' The order number IS the office door code.
Order #1953 from Moretti's Hardware. Quickite — that's quickite, lye-grade calcium oxide. For dissolving things. The order number is the office door code.

items.name: Butcher Knife
items.description: A ten-inch carbon steel blade. This is a professional tool.

then.text: Honed to a razor edge. The handle is worn smooth from years of use. There are notches cut into the base of the blade — seven of them.

items.name: Desk Drawer Key
items.description: A small brass key. Found taped under the cash register.

then.text: Tiny brass key. A strip of masking tape on it reads 'DESK' in block letters.

items.name: Black Book
items.description: Sal's private ledger. Names, dates, amounts. This is the kind of book people kill for.

then.text: Pages of entries. Dates, dollar amounts, names — some you recognize from the news. Capo Vincenzo Deluca. Tony 'Two-Tone' Ricci. The last entry: your name, tonight's date, a dollar amount, and the word 'HANDLED.' This is enough to put Sal away. Or enough to make him very cooperative.
Sal's book of sins. Every dirty dollar, every dirty deed. Your ticket out — or a death sentence if he catches you with it.

items.name: Polaroid Photos
items.description: A stack of Polaroids that should never have been taken.

then.text: Six Polaroids. Men in suits shaking hands with Sal. Money changing hands. One photo shows a city councilman. Another shows the back of this shop — and a body being loaded into a trunk. Dates on the backs. This is evidence of murder, bribery, and racketeering.
Sal's insurance policy. If these photos got to the right people, a lot of powerful men would fall.

items.name: Chain Link Piece
items.description: A section of chain cut from the loading dock hoist.

then.text: About two feet of heavy chain. Could wrap around something, or wedge into a mechanism.

items.name: Ceramic Fuse
items.description: A cylindrical ceramic fuse pulled from the panel.

then.text: Old-style ceramic fuse cylinder. Labeled 'MAIN FLOOR - 30A'. Without this, the shop floor goes dark.

items.name: Newspaper
items.description: Today's Chicago Tribune, folded to the local section.

then.text: 'MISSING PERSONS CASES MOUNT IN SOUTH SIDE' — Three disappearances in six months, all last seen near Morano's Meats. Below the fold: an ad for Morano's. 'Fresh cuts daily. Family owned since 1952.' A phone number for orders is listed. Scrawled in pen next to the ad: 'Tony — call after 11pm. 555-0134.'
The Tribune. Three missing persons. Tony's number: 555-0134.

items.name: Fire Extinguisher
items.description: A heavy red cylinder. Could put out fires — or create a distraction.

then.text: Heavy-duty dry chemical extinguisher. The pin is still in. Pull it and squeeze — you'd fill a room with white powder. Instant smoke screen.

items.name: Delivery Schedule
items.description: A clipboard page showing this week's deliveries.

then.text: Chicago Wholesale Meats — delivery schedule. Tonight: 'PICKUP 11:45 PM — Loading Dock B.' That's this dock. If a truck comes, the roll-up door has to open.

items.name: Crowbar
items.description: A short iron crowbar from behind the boxes.

then.text: About 18 inches. Solid iron. Good for prying, breaking, and leverage.

items.name: Sal's Wallet
items.description: A fat leather wallet. Sal's personal effects.

then.text: Driver's license — Salvatore Morano, 2847 S. Halsted. A thick roll of twenties. A photo of a woman and two kids. Behind it, a slip of paper: 'Wall safe — Angela's birthday. 10-17.' The combination to his wall safe.
You pocket the cash. Might need it. The photo of his family stares up at you.

items.name: Evidence Package
items.description: The ledger and photos organized into a damning case against Sal and his associates.

then.text: Dates, names, dollar amounts — each photo matched to a ledger entry. Payoffs to judges, cops, union bosses. This could put Sal and half the Outfit away.

items.name: Hook and Chain
items.description: A meat hook threaded with chain. A crude grapple — or a vicious weapon.

then.text: The chain loops through the hook's eye, knotted tight. You could swing this, throw it, or hook it onto something overhead.

items.name: Reinforced Pry Bar
items.description: A crowbar wrapped with chain for extra leverage. Could break a lock.

then.text: The chain is wound tight around the crowbar's shaft. The extra weight and grip give it serious prying power. A padlock wouldn't stand a chance.

items.name: Wrapped Blade
items.description: A butcher knife with the apron wrapped around the handle for a better, quieter grip.

then.text: The apron fabric dampens any clatter when you set it down. The blade is still razor sharp — Sal keeps his tools in order.

combinations.message: You organize the photos alongside the ledger entries they match. Dates, names, amounts — it all lines up. This is an airtight case.
You thread the chain through the hook's eye and loop it tight. A crude grapple — or a nasty trap.
You wrap the chain around the crowbar for extra leverage. This could break a lock.
You wrap the apron around the blade handle for a better grip, and muffle the sound when you set it down.

objects.name: Freezer Door
objects.description: Heavy insulated steel. The handle is on the outside.

then.text: A walk-in freezer door, thick as a bank vault's. The latch is on the outside. No handle on this side — just smooth steel and frost. But the hinges... the hinges are on the inside. Three of them, held by bolts thick with ice.
You pound on the door. It doesn't budge. The cold burns your fists.
"Hey! HEY! Let me out!" The whistling stops. Then, muffled through the steel: "Shut up in there. I'm working." The whistling resumes.

You work the hook's point into the icy hinge bolts. They're frozen solid but the hook finds purchase. Cracking, scraping — the top bolt breaks free. The middle one. The bottom. The door sags on its latch, and you shoulder it open into the shop. Warm air hits you like a wall.
You jam the crowbar under the hinge plate and heave. The ice cracks, the bolts shear. One hinge, two, three — the door groans open. Stale warmth floods in.
You try to work the blade into the hinge gap. The steel is too thick — the knife just scrapes uselessly. You'd need something with more leverage.
The freezer door hangs open on its broken hinges. Cold air leaks out. Beyond it — the shop.

objects.name: Meat Hooks
objects.description: A row of steel hooks on an overhead rail.

then.text: Eight steel hooks on a rail that runs the length of the ceiling. Most hold frozen carcasses. One at the end is empty, low enough to reach.
You wrench the empty hook off its rail. It comes free with a screech of metal. Heavy, sharp, and cold as death.
You already have one. The rest are holding up two hundred pounds of beef each.

objects.name: Metal Shelving
objects.description: Industrial shelving lined with wrapped cuts and labeled boxes.

then.text: Steel shelving crammed with labeled parcels. Pork shoulders, chuck rolls, briskets. On the bottom shelf, shoved behind a tray of ribs — a brown paper bag that doesn't match the others.
You pull out the brown bag. Inside: a wallet. Sal must have stashed it here by habit — butchers don't carry wallets on the floor.
Just meat and packaging. Nothing else hidden here.

objects.name: Hanging Carcasses
objects.description: Frozen sides of beef sway gently on their hooks.

messages: Four half-carcasses hang from hooks, frost-rimed and still. They sway slightly in the freezer's circulation. You try not to think about who was here before you.
Sides of beef. Some pork. All frozen solid, white with frost. The hooks creak overhead.
Frozen meat hangs from the rail. The gaps between the carcasses are just wide enough for a person to stand in.

then.text: You push a carcass aside. It swings heavily, chain clinking. Behind it — nothing but more cold wall.

objects.name: Gap Between Carcasses
objects.description: A narrow space between the frozen beef. You could squeeze in.

then.text: A narrow gap between two frozen carcasses. Dark, cold, and tight — but a person could fit. The frost would hide your breath.
You squeeze between the frozen carcasses. The cold is brutal, pressing through your clothes. But you're invisible — just another shape in the dark.
You squeeze out from between the carcasses, gasping. Your body aches from the cold.

objects.name: Floor Drain
objects.description: A large circular drain in the concrete floor.

then.text: A heavy iron drain grate set into the concrete. Stained dark. You don't want to think about what's gone down there. The grate is bolted down.
The grate won't budge. Bolted tight. Even if you could open it, the pipe looks too narrow for a person.
You pry at the grate. It lifts an inch — the pipe below is maybe six inches wide. No way out, but you can see a glint of metal caught on the grate's underside. A brass key, snagged on the ironwork.

objects.name: Ventilation Grate
objects.description: An air vent high on the wall, frosted over.

then.text: A ventilation duct opening, about 10 inches square. Too small to crawl through. Cold air blows in from the refrigeration unit. You can hear the shop through it — Sal's whistling, the radio playing Sinatra.
You press your ear to the vent. Sal is talking to himself: '...one more hour, then I clean up. Nobody's gonna miss this one...' The radio switches to a news report about the missing persons.
You pry at the grate with your fingers. It rattles but holds. The screws are rusted but could be forced with a tool.
You use the hook to pry the screws. They pop out one by one. The grate comes free. The duct is too small to enter, but now you can hear everything Sal does — and the sound carries both ways.

objects.name: Fuse Panel
objects.description: An old electrical panel mounted on the wall.

then.text: An old fuse panel, the kind with screw-in ceramic cylinders. The door is latched shut with a simple hook.
You unhook the latch and swing the panel open. Inside: rows of ceramic fuses. One is labeled 'MAIN FLOOR' in faded marker. Pull it and the shop goes dark.

You unscrew the MAIN FLOOR fuse. It comes free in your hand. Instantly, you hear the shop lights die through the vent — and Sal cursing in the dark. 'What the — fuses again? This goddamn building...' He stumbles toward the breaker box.
The fuse socket is empty. The shop is running on whatever circuits are left.

objects.name: Mop Bucket
objects.description: A wheeled mop bucket with murky water.

then.text: Industrial mop bucket on wheels. The water is pink. A mop handle sticks up from the wringer. The bucket itself is heavy steel — wheel it into a doorway and it'd slow someone down.
You wheel the bucket. It squeaks across the floor. This could block a path — or make a hell of a noise if someone trips on it.

objects.name: Cardboard Boxes
objects.description: A stack of supply boxes in the corner.

then.text: Cardboard supply boxes stacked high. 'Chicago Wholesale Meats' stamped on the side. Something heavy is propped behind them, leaning against the wall.
You shift the boxes aside. Behind them — a short iron crowbar, forgotten or stashed.
Just empty boxes and dust.

objects.name: Apron Hook
objects.description: A hook by the door with a hanging apron.

then.text: A butcher's apron hanging on a steel hook. Stiff with dried blood. There's a breast pocket with something in it.
You pull the apron off the hook. It's stiff and stinking, but there's definitely something in the pocket.

objects.name: Wall Thermometer
objects.description: An industrial thermometer mounted by the door.

then.text: The thermometer reads -5°F. Your breath crystallizes instantly. You can't stay in here much longer.
The thermometer reads -5°F. Your fingers are going numb. Your thoughts are getting sluggish. You NEED to get out of this freezer.

objects.name: Cutting Board
objects.description: A massive butcher block, scarred from years of use.

then.text: An enormous butcher block, three inches thick. Deep cuts groove its surface. Fresh blood in the grain. A half-wrapped brisket sits to one side. Under the block, a shelf holds cutting tools.
You feel under the block's shelf. Your fingers find the smooth handle of a wrapped blade.

objects.name: Knife Rack
objects.description: A magnetic strip on the wall holding an array of knives.

then.text: Six knives on a magnetic strip: boning knife, cleaver, fillet knife, chef's knife, butcher knife, and a small paring knife. All impeccably maintained. The butcher knife is the biggest — ten inches of carbon steel.
You ease the butcher knife off the magnetic strip. It comes free with a quiet snap. Ten inches of razor-sharp steel. Sal will notice it's gone.
You already have the best knife. The rest are too specialized to be useful.

objects.name: Meat Grinder
objects.description: An industrial meat grinder bolted to the counter.

then.text: A commercial Hobart grinder. Heavy, steel, bolted to the counter. The power switch is on the side. When running, this thing would be LOUD — drowning out any other sound in the shop.

You flip the switch. The grinder roars to life — a deafening industrial grinding that fills the shop. Sal shouts from the back: 'What the hell?!' and comes running. You've got maybe thirty seconds while he's dealing with it.

effects.text: The grinder shuts off. Sal's voice: 'Damn thing's got a mind of its own.' Silence returns to the shop.

then.text: The grinder is running full tilt. The noise is tremendous. Whatever you do right now, Sal won't hear it.

objects.name: Cash Register
objects.description: An old brass National register.

then.text: A brass National cash register, the old kind with the ornate scrollwork. The drawer is closed. Something is taped underneath it — you'd have to reach under to check.
You reach under the register. Your fingers find a small key taped to the bottom. You peel it free.
Nothing else under the register. The drawer is locked anyway.

objects.name: Order Pad
objects.description: A carbon-copy order pad by the register.

then.text: Carbon-copy order forms. The top sheet has today's date. A list of cuts with customer names. The last entry is different — no name, just 'SPECIAL ORDER — 180 lbs — PICKUP MIDNIGHT — CASH ONLY.' Somebody's buying a body's worth of meat at midnight.

objects.name: Wall Calendar
objects.description: A 1974 calendar with a pin-up girl for October.

then.text: October 1974. A Marilyn Monroe knock-off in a butcher's apron. Today's date is circled in red. Written in the margin: 'Angela's birthday — 10/17. Don't forget flowers. Hide briefcase before party.' Angela's birthday is October 17th — 10-17.
October 1974. Angela's birthday is the 17th — 10/17. The briefcase note is suggestive.

objects.name: Wall Phone
objects.description: A rotary wall phone by the counter.

then.text: A rotary wall phone, avocado green. The cord reaches about six feet. This is the public shop phone — Sal might hear you if you pick it up.
You lift the receiver. Dial tone. But Sal is too close — he'd hear you talking. You need a distraction first.
Sal is distracted. You pick up the receiver. Dial tone. Who do you call?
You dial 911. 'Chicago Police, what's your emergency?' You whisper the address, Sal's name, the murders — everything. 'Stay on the line, units are en route.' Sirens in the distance. Growing louder.

effects.text: Red and blue lights flood through the windows. Sal screams. Doors crash. 'CHICAGO PD! ON THE GROUND!' It's over. You're safe. The evidence in your hands will put Sal Morano away for life.

effects.reason: You called the police with ironclad evidence. Sal Morano is arrested for murder, racketeering, and conspiracy. The black book names names — half the South Side mob goes down with him. You walk out of that shop alive, and a dozen cold cases finally get answers.

then.text: You dial 555-0134. Two rings. A gravel voice: 'Yeah?' You talk fast — Sal's got you locked up, you've got his book, every name and number. Long silence. 'Stay put. I'm sending someone.' The line goes dead.

You dial 911. 'Chicago Police, what's your emergency?' You whisper the address and that you're being held. 'We'll send a unit, stay calm.' But without evidence, it'll be your word against his — and Sal has friends on the force.

objects.name: Display Case
objects.description: A glass-front refrigerated display case for the shop front.

then.text: A glass-fronted refrigerated case. Steaks, chops, and sausages on white trays. The back panel slides open — the case is deep enough to curl up inside.
You slide the back panel open and squeeze in among the cold cuts. Through the glass, you can see the whole shop floor. Humiliating, but effective.
You slide out from the display case, bits of butcher paper stuck to your clothes.

objects.name: Sawdust Floor
objects.description: The shop floor is covered in sawdust.

then.text: Fresh sawdust on the concrete floor. Traditional butcher shop practice — absorbs blood and fluids. Your footprints are visible in it. Sal will see them.
You scuff the sawdust to obscure your footprints. It helps, but the trail from the freezer door is obvious.

objects.name: Newspaper
objects.description: Today's Chicago Tribune on the counter.

then.text: The Chicago Tribune, today's date. Folded to an article: 'MISSING PERSONS CASES MOUNT IN SOUTH SIDE — Third disappearance in six months.' Below: an ad for Morano's Meats with a phone number.
You grab the newspaper. The missing persons article and the scrawled phone number could both be useful.

objects.name: Office Desk
objects.description: A heavy oak desk covered in paperwork.

then.text: An oak desk piled with invoices, tax forms, and food safety certificates. The center drawer has a small brass lock. Under the glass desktop protector, a family photo and a business card for 'Anthony Ricci — Import/Export.'
The drawer is locked. A small brass keyhole.
The key turns smoothly. Inside the drawer: a .38 revolver (no bullets), a stack of twenties, and a black leather book.
You jam the hook into the keyhole and twist. The cheap lock gives way with a crack. Inside: a revolver, cash, and a black leather book.

objects.name: Filing Cabinet
objects.description: A green metal filing cabinet.

then.text: A four-drawer filing cabinet. Unlocked. The labels read: INVOICES, SUPPLIERS, EMPLOYEES, PERSONAL.
You open the PERSONAL drawer. Manila folders stuffed with documents. One labeled 'INSURANCE' holds an envelope marked 'DO NOT OPEN.' Inside: six Polaroid photographs.
The rest is boring — tax returns, supplier agreements, employee records. Nothing useful.

objects.name: Desk Phone
objects.description: A rotary phone on the desk.

then.text: A black rotary phone on the desk. The office door is thick — if it's closed, Sal might not hear a conversation.

You pick up the receiver and dial 911. The operator patches you through. You give them everything — the address, Sal's name, the murders, the mob connections. You describe the evidence you're holding. 'Stay where you are. Units en route.' The office door muffles your voice. Sal doesn't hear a thing.

effects.text: Sirens wail outside. Car doors. Pounding. 'POLICE! OPEN UP!' Sal's panicked footsteps. 'No — no no NO—' The front door splinters. You step out of the office, evidence in hand, into a wall of badges and flashlights. It's over.

effects.reason: You called the police from the back office with a mountain of evidence. Sal Morano is arrested. The black book and photographs trigger a RICO investigation that dismantles half the South Side organization. You're the star witness — and you walk out alive.

then.text: You dial 555-0134. One ring. 'Who is this?' You explain: you're in Sal's shop, you have his book, and if Tony doesn't send a car in fifteen minutes, the book goes to the Tribune. Dead silence. Then: 'Don't move.' Click.
The office door is locked. You can't get to the phone.

objects.name: Leather Briefcase
objects.description: A fine leather briefcase under the desk.

then.text: A high-quality leather briefcase tucked under the desk. It has a four-dial combination lock. The dials show 0-0-0-0.
Locked. Four-dial combination. You'd need the code.
The briefcase is open. Empty now — you already took what was inside.

objects.name: Painting
objects.description: A cheap landscape painting on the wall.

then.text: A cheap landscape — rolling hills, a sunset. The frame is slightly crooked, like it's been moved recently. Classic hiding spot.
You swing the painting aside. Behind it — a wall safe with a combination dial. Two numbers, separated by a dash.

objects.name: Wall Safe
objects.description: A steel wall safe behind the painting.

then.text: A Sargent & Greenleaf wall safe. Combination dial — two-number combination, it looks like. Turn right to the first number, left to the second.
Angela's birthday — 10-17. You spin the dial. Right to 10. Left to 17. Click. The door swings open. Inside: a thick manila envelope and $5,000 in cash.
The envelope contains duplicate records — carbon copies of every page in the black book, plus negatives of the Polaroids. Sal's backup insurance.
You try random numbers. Nothing. You'd need to know the combination.

objects.name: Coat Rack
objects.description: A wooden coat rack with Sal's overcoat.

then.text: Sal's heavy wool overcoat hangs here. A hat on the top hook.
You search the coat pockets. A pack of Luckys, a lighter, some change. Nothing useful — but the coat itself is heavy. If you threw it over someone's head...

objects.name: Waste Basket
objects.description: A metal waste basket under the desk.

then.text: Crumpled papers, a coffee cup, cigar butts. One crumpled paper catches your eye — it has numbers on it.

You smooth out the crumpled paper. It's a draft page from the black book with corrections. One entry is circled: 'Briefcase combo — use the hardware order #.' If you have the receipt, you have the combo.
Nothing else in the trash.

objects.name: Open Ledger
objects.description: A large accounting ledger open on the desk.

then.text: The legitimate business ledger — meat sales, expenses, payroll. But some line items are suspicious: 'Special handling fee — $2000.' 'Disposal service — $1500.' 'Consultation — $5000.' All cash. None of these are normal butcher expenses.
The shop ledger. Suspicious entries, but nothing as damning as the black book.

objects.name: Family Photo
objects.description: A framed photograph on the desk.

then.text: Sal with a woman and two kids. The woman's smile is forced. The kids look scared. On the frame's base, engraved: 'Angela, Maria, Little Sal — 1972.' A normal family. One with a monster in it.

objects.name: Office Window
objects.description: A frosted glass window looking onto the alley.

then.text: Frosted glass, iron-framed. Through it, the blurred shapes of the alley — dumpster, fire escape across the way. The window is painted shut and barred on the outside.
Painted shut. Even if you could open it, the bars outside would stop you.

objects.name: Roll-Up Door
objects.description: A metal roll-up door for deliveries.

then.text: A heavy steel roll-up door. Padlocked at the bottom with a chain running through the handle and a floor anchor. The chain is thick but the padlock looks old.
The chain rattles when you pull. Solid. The padlock won't budge with bare hands.
You jam the reinforced crowbar into the padlock and heave with everything you have. The chain-wrapped leverage does it — the shackle snaps. The chain falls away.
You try to pry the padlock. The crowbar slips — not enough leverage on its own. You'd need something to wrap around it for a better grip.
A knife won't cut chain. You need leverage, not an edge.
You grab the handle and heave the door up. It screeches on its tracks, rolling upward. Cold night air rushes in. The alley is right there — freedom. You duck under and run.

then.reason: You break the chain and haul up the loading dock door. The alley is dark and empty. You run — past the dumpsters, past the parked trucks, out onto Halsted Street and into the night. Sal Morano will know you escaped, but by then you'll be long gone. Whether you took his secrets with you or left them behind — that's between you and your conscience.

objects.name: Chain Hoist
objects.description: An overhead chain hoist for moving heavy deliveries.

then.text: An industrial chain hoist on a ceiling rail. Heavy-duty, meant for swinging carcass-sized loads around the dock. The chain hangs loose. You could rig this as a trap — or cut a piece of chain from it.

You hook the chain-and-hook onto the hoist's release mechanism and position it over the doorway. When Sal walks through, you pull the release — 30 pounds of steel drops on him. A dirty trick, but you're fighting dirty.
You saw at a weak link in the hanging chain. The knife isn't ideal but the link was already corroded. It parts with a snap. You now have a length of chain.
You use the hook to pry apart a corroded link. The chain separates and you grab a section.

objects.name: Pallet Stack
objects.description: Wooden shipping pallets stacked against the wall.

then.text: Wooden pallets stacked five high. There's a gap behind them — not comfortable, but you could squeeze in and pull a pallet across.
You squeeze behind the pallets and pull one across the gap. Splinters dig into your back, but you're hidden.
You push the pallet aside and climb out, pulling splinters from your shirt.

objects.name: Delivery Clipboard
objects.description: A clipboard hanging by the roll-up door.

then.text: Delivery schedules for the week. Tonight has a late pickup marked: '11:45 PM — Chicago Wholesale.' The truck will need the roll-up door opened.
You tear off the schedule page. The delivery time could be useful.

objects.name: Circuit Breaker Box
objects.description: A more modern breaker box on the dock wall.

then.text: A secondary breaker panel for the loading dock. Labeled switches: DOCK LIGHTS, HOIST POWER, ROLL-UP MOTOR, ALARM. The ALARM breaker has a red tag.
You flip open the panel. The breakers are all in the ON position. Flipping ROLL-UP MOTOR would disable the electric door opener — Sal couldn't close it remotely.

objects.name: Fire Extinguisher
objects.description: A red fire extinguisher mounted on the wall.

then.text: A heavy dry-chemical fire extinguisher. Could fill a room with white powder in seconds — instant visual cover.
You lift the extinguisher off its mount. Heavy — maybe fifteen pounds. Pull the pin and squeeze.

objects.name: Side Door
objects.description: A steel door leading to the alley.

then.text: A steel fire door. A deadbolt lock — needs a key from either side. Sal has the only key. No picking this one.
Deadbolted. Without Sal's key, this door isn't opening.

A car horn blares outside. Headlights flash through the frosted glass. Tony sent his people. You spray the extinguisher at the door hinges — the rapid cooling on heated metal weakens them. One kick, two — the door bursts outward. A black Lincoln idles in the alley. The passenger door opens. 'Get in. Now.' You clutch the black book to your chest and climb in.

then.reason: You blackmailed Tony Ricci with Sal's own evidence, and Tony sent a car. The Lincoln takes you downtown, where a nervous lawyer offers you a deal: your silence about what you know, a new identity, and a one-way ticket out of Chicago. You take it. Sal Morano is found floating in the river two weeks later. You never find out if that was justice or just the mob cleaning up. Either way, you're alive.

objects.name: Dumpster
objects.description: A large commercial dumpster by the loading dock.

then.text: A six-yard commercial dumpster. The lid is heavy but not locked. The smell is... educational. But it's big enough to hide in.
You lift the lid and climb in among the refuse. Rotting meat trimmings, fat, and bone. The smell is beyond description. But you're invisible.
You haul yourself out of the dumpster, gagging. You'll never eat a hamburger again.

on_solve.text: The keypad beeps. The office door lock clicks open. You're in.

on_fail.text: Wrong code. The keypad buzzes angrily.

on_max_fail.text: The keypad locks out and emits a sustained alarm tone. Sal's voice from the back: 'What the hell is going on out there?!'

on_solve.text: Click. The latches spring open. Inside the briefcase: a bundle of $100 bills and a sealed envelope marked 'LEVERAGE — OPEN ONLY IF NEEDED.' The envelope contains more Polaroids — worse than the others.
The right combination: hoist power ON to use the chain trap, roll-up motor OFF so Sal can't close it remotely, dock lights OFF for darkness, alarm OFF so you don't trip it. Smart.

then.text: The breakers click but nothing helpful happens.

else.text: You already set the breakers correctly.

phases.name: Hypothermia Setting In

on_enter.text: Cold. You're so cold. Your fingers are stiff, your breath is a white cloud. How long have you been in here? The freezer hums. Through the walls, Sal whistles. Think. Focus. Get out of this freezer before the cold takes you.

phases.ambient_text: The freezer thrums. Your teeth chatter. Sal's whistling filters through the walls.

phases.name: The Shop Floor

on_enter.text: You're out of the freezer. The shop stretches before you — butcher counter, display cases, the smell of raw meat and sawdust. A radio plays Sinatra. Somewhere deeper in the building, Sal works. An office door at the back has a keypad lock. The loading dock is through a wide archway. Move quietly.

phases.ambient_text: Sinatra croons on the radio. Sal's cleaver hits the block. The clock ticks toward midnight.

phases.name: Closing Time

on_enter.text: Sal's scream cuts through the shop: 'WHERE IS IT?! WHERE'S MY BOOK?! I'LL GUT YOU LIKE A PIG!' Heavy footsteps. He knows. He knows everything. The hunt is on.

phases.ambient_text: Sal is tearing the shop apart. Crashes. Screaming. He's lost all composure.

effects.text: Your fingers are going numb. Your thinking is getting foggy. Hypothermia is setting in. You need to get out of this freezer NOW.
You can barely feel your hands. Your vision is tunneling. The cold is killing you — slowly, quietly. If you don't get out in the next minute, you won't get out at all.
The cold stops hurting. That's the worst sign. You slide down the wall, too tired to shiver. Your last thought is that the freezer hum sounds almost peaceful...

effects.reason: Hypothermia. You spent too long in the walk-in freezer and succumbed to the cold. Sal found you the next morning, stiff and blue. Another disappearance on the South Side.

effects.text: The shop phone rings. Sal answers: 'Yeah... No, it's handled... Midnight pickup like always... Look, Tony, I said it's HANDLED. Don't worry about it.' He hangs up hard.
Sal mutters to himself and goes back to work. The distraction is over.
Sal's routine check turns into a frenzy. He sees the desk drawer open, the book gone. The calm facade shatters.
Engine rumble outside. Headlights sweep across the loading dock windows. A truck horn blares twice. The midnight delivery has arrived — Sal will have to open the loading dock door.
The truck pulls away. Sal closes the loading dock. The window is gone.

messages: Through the wall you hear Sal: 'Now, Mrs. Henderson, you wanted the crown roast, didn't you? Let's get you looking pretty...' He's talking to a cut of meat. Like it's a customer.
Sal's voice drifts through the shop: 'Beautiful. Just beautiful. Look at those marbling lines. You're gonna make someone very happy tomorrow, sweetheart.' He's talking to a steak.
You hear Sal humming, then: 'Don't worry, I'll take good care of you. Just like all the others.' A cleaver comes down. Hard.

killer.name: Sal Morano
killer.description: A barrel-chested man in his fifties, thick arms, slicked-back hair going gray. He's been a butcher for thirty years and a killer for nearly as long. He talks to the meat, whistles while he works, and approaches violence with the same methodical calm he brings to breaking down a side of beef.

on_approach: Time to check on my guest...
You better still be where I left you.
Let me see how our special order is doing.
on_search: I know you're in here. I can smell the fear on you.
Come on out. Let's talk about this like men.
You think you can hide from me? In MY shop?
I've been finding things in this shop for thirty years. You're not that hard to find.
on_evidence: What the — who's been in my office?!
You touched my things. Nobody touches my things.
Oh, you're gonna wish you stayed in that freezer.
on_catch: There you are. I was hoping we could do this the easy way.
Found you. Now — you wanna know what a butcher does with a problem? He breaks it down into smaller pieces.
End of the line, friend. Let's go to the back room.

effects.text: Sal slams the freezer door shut and chains it. You hear him cursing.
Sal notices the missing knife. 'Where's my ten-inch? Son of a...' His searches will be more thorough now.
Sal sees the forced drawer. His face goes white, then red. 'THE BOOK! WHERE'S MY BOOK?!'

special_behaviors.description: Sal rushes to shut off the meat grinder.
Sal stumbles in the dark looking for the fuse box.

win_conditions.description: Call the police with assembled evidence
Break out through the loading dock
Blackmail Tony Ricci with Sal's evidence

lose_conditions.description: Died of hypothermia in the freezer

hints.text: The freezer door's hinges are on the inside. Something sharp and strong could work on the hinge bolts — especially if they're frozen and brittle.
Search the freezer carefully. An empty meat hook could be pulled from the rail. There might also be something hidden behind the boxes in the corner.
The office door has a keypad. The code might be hidden somewhere in the freezer — on a receipt or document Sal left in his work apron.
The wall safe behind the painting needs a combination. Think about what's important to Sal — check the calendar and his personal effects.
To call the police effectively, you need real evidence. The filing cabinet's PERSONAL drawer and the locked desk drawer both hold damning material. Combine what you find.
The meat grinder makes enough noise to cover a phone call. And pulling the main floor fuse plunges the shop into darkness.
The loading dock roll-up door is padlocked with a chain. A crowbar alone isn't enough leverage — but what if you reinforced it?
The newspaper has a phone number for someone named Tony. If you had Sal's black book and called Tony with the right leverage, you might be able to arrange an... exit.

solution_paths.name: The Right Thing (Police Rescue)
solution_paths.description: Gather ironclad evidence and call the police. The lawful path — put Sal away for life.
steps: Take the meat hook from the rail
Take the apron from the hook, search it for the receipt
Examine the receipt to learn the office code (1953)
Use the meat hook on the freezer door hinges to escape
Navigate to the butcher counter view
Enter code 1953 on the office keypad
In the office: search the filing cabinet for Polaroid photos
Search the waste basket for the ledger clue (briefcase combo = order number)
Use the office key on the desk drawer to get the black book
OR: Use meat hook to force the desk drawer
Combine the black book with the Polaroids to create evidence_package
Create a distraction (turn on meat grinder OR pull the main floor fuse)
While Sal is distracted, use the desk phone or counter phone to call 911
Wait for police to arrive

solution_paths.name: The Hard Way (Loading Dock Escape)
solution_paths.description: Smash your way out through the loading dock. The loud, direct path.
steps: Take the meat hook from the rail
Find the crowbar behind the cardboard boxes
Use the meat hook or crowbar on the freezer door to escape
Navigate to the loading dock view
Cut chain from the hoist (use butcher_knife or meat_hook on chain_hoist)
Combine the crowbar with the chain to make reinforced_pry_bar
Use the reinforced_pry_bar on the roll-up door padlock
Open the unchained roll-up door to escape into the alley

solution_paths.name: The Deal (Blackmail Escape)
solution_paths.description: Use Sal's own secrets against the mob. The morally gray path — make a deal with the devil.
steps: Take the meat hook and escape the freezer
Take the newspaper from the counter — learn Tony's phone number (555-0134)
Get the office code from the apron receipt and enter the office
Get the black book from the desk drawer
Create a distraction to use a phone safely
Call Tony (555-0134) from the desk phone or counter phone with the black book
Wait for Tony to send a car
Take the fire extinguisher from the loading dock
When the car arrives, use the fire extinguisher on the alley door to break out
Climb into the waiting Lincoln
